claims.title: Shopper order details may be intercepted if the public checkout flow lacks transport encryption
claims.description: `flow:entity:shopper>process:storefront-api>place-order` crosses from `boundary:public-internet` to `boundary:storefront-dmz` and carries shopper PII and financial order data, including shipping addresses and card last-four, but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If that unknown resolves to no effective TLS protection, an attacker able to observe the public path can intercept the submitted order data before it reaches `process:storefront-api`. The disclosed address, order contents, and payment metadata enable targeted fraud and social-engineering attacks against the affected shopper. This is conditional on verifying the transport protection; it does not assert that the flow is cleartext.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high and conditional because `flow:entity:shopper>process:storefront-api>place-order` crosses the public-internet boundary and its transport encryption is unverified. Impact is high because the flow carries `pii` and `financial` order details for internet-facing checkout users.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce TLS for checkout submissions
mitigations.detail: Require TLS 1.2+ on `flow:entity:shopper>process:storefront-api>place-order`, record the verified protocol and `encryption_in_transit` state, and reject plaintext HTTP.

mitigations.summary: Minimize payment metadata in the order submission
mitigations.detail: Use payment-provider references rather than transmitting payment-related fields beyond those required for checkout.

claims.title: Settlement callback contents may be intercepted if webhook transport protection is absent
claims.description: `flow:entity:card-processor>process:storefront-api>settlement-webhook` crosses from `boundary:public-internet` to `process:storefront-api`, carries financial settlement confirmations, and has unknown protocol and `encryption_in_transit`. If transport encryption is absent or ineffective, an on-path observer can intercept settlement status and order-payment metadata sent by `entity:card-processor`. That disclosure reveals which orders were paid and can enable targeted fraud against shoppers and payment operations. This is conditional on the unresolved transport attributes.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high and conditional because the webhook crosses the public-internet boundary while its protocol and transport encryption are unverified. Impact is medium because the modeled flow carries financial settlement confirmation data, but the described payload is narrower than the complete order and address record.

mitigations.summary: Require HTTPS/TLS for the processor webhook
mitigations.detail: Configure `flow:entity:card-processor>process:storefront-api>settlement-webhook` to use verified TLS and explicitly record its protocol and `encryption_in_transit` posture.
Transmit an opaque settlement reference where possible and have `process:storefront-api` retrieve only the necessary settlement details through a protected processor integration.

claims.title: Orders crossing from the storefront to the core may be readable if gRPC transport encryption is absent
claims.description: `flow:process:storefront-api>process:order-service>submit-order` crosses from `boundary:storefront-dmz` to `boundary:core-services` and forwards order contents, shopper identifiers, and shipping addresses. Its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If the gRPC transport is not protected, an attacker with observation capability on that inter-zone path can intercept PII and financial order data in transit. The disclosed shopper identifiers and order details can then be used to target customers and correlate records later stored in `store:orders-db`. This is conditional on the unresolved encryption attribute.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because observing the DMZ-to-core path requires a foothold on that internal route, although `encryption_in_transit` is unverified. Impact is high because the flow carries both `pii` and `financial` data for submitted orders.

mitigations.summary: Use mTLS on the storefront-to-order-service gRPC call
mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` for `flow:process:storefront-api>process:order-service>submit-order` to mutually authenticated TLS so order payloads are confidential on the DMZ-to-core hop.

mitigations.summary: Reduce sensitive fields on the internal message
mitigations.detail: Send an opaque order reference where `process:order-service` can retrieve required details through a separately protected, least-privilege path.

claims.title: Order database traffic may expose shopper records if its internal connection is unencrypted
claims.description: `flow:process:order-service>store:orders-db>read-write-orders` carries order rows, shipping addresses, and card last-four between `process:order-service` and confidential `store:orders-db`, but its protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the database connection lacks effective encryption, an attacker able to observe this internal path can intercept the records while the order service reads or writes them. The captured data can be correlated with the corpus in `store:orders-db` and used to target affected shoppers. This is conditional on verifying the database transport configuration.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because an attacker must first gain an observation position on the internal order-service-to-database path, although the transport controls are unverified. Impact is high because `store:orders-db` is confidential and the flow carries `pii` and `financial` order records.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and authenticate the database connection
mitigations.detail: Require TLS for `flow:process:order-service>store:orders-db>read-write-orders`, validate the database certificate, and record the protocol and `encryption_in_transit` state.
Segment the order-service and database network path and limit packet-capture and network-administration access to separately authorized operators.

claims.title: A copied orders database may disclose all shopper records if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:orders-db` is classified confidential and holds PII and financial data, including shopper addresses and card last-four, but `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If that attribute resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker who obtains a database volume, decommissioned medium, operational snapshot, or backup copy can read the stored order corpus without authenticating through `process:order-service`. The resulting corpus enables broad targeting and correlation of shoppers and their purchase history. This is a conditional storage-copy threat, not an assertion that `store:orders-db` is currently unencrypted.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown `encryption_at_rest` state: obtaining an operational copy requires storage-layer access, but an unencrypted copy needs no application credential. Impact is high because `store:orders-db` is confidential and holds corpus-scale `pii` and `financial` records.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encryption at rest for orders data
mitigations.detail: Establish the actual `encryption_at_rest` state of `store:orders-db`, then require managed-key or customer-managed-key encryption for database media and every operational backup, snapshot, and replica.
Restrict export, snapshot, backup, and decommissioning workflows to dedicated principals and maintain auditable handling of storage media.

claims.title: Database password stored in the order-service environment can unlock the orders corpus
claims.description: The application-account password used on `flow:process:order-service>store:orders-db>read-write-orders` is kept in an environment variable on `process:order-service`, and the application account has full read/write access to `store:orders-db`. An attacker who recovers that credential from the worker's environment can use it to query the confidential orders database and read all shopper addresses and card last-four rather than only one order. This enables corpus-scale profiling and targeted fraud against the shoppers represented in the database.

quotes.text: The password comes from an environment variable on the worker.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because the attacker must recover the credential from `process:order-service`, but the stated environment-variable custody creates a standing secret to obtain. Impact is high because the application account has stated full read/write access to confidential `store:orders-db`, which contains `pii` and `financial` data.

mitigations.summary: Replace the environment password with short-lived workload credentials
mitigations.detail: Use workload identity or a dedicated secret manager with rotation for the database connection so `process:order-service` does not retain a long-lived password in its environment.

mitigations.summary: Reduce the application account's read scope
mitigations.detail: Replace the full read/write grant with roles limited to the required tables, columns, and operations, so a recovered credential cannot expose the whole order corpus.

claims.title: Code running in the order service inherits full read access to confidential orders
claims.description: `process:order-service` reads and writes `store:orders-db` through `flow:process:order-service>store:orders-db>read-write-orders` using an application account with full read/write access. An attacker who gains code execution in `process:order-service` can use that existing database session or credential to read the full confidential order corpus, including shopper addresses and card last-four. Encryption at rest would not prevent this read because the authorized database connection decrypts records for the service. The disclosure enables bulk shopper profiling and targeted fraud, rather than being limited to the attacker’s own order.

quotes.text: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because the attacker must first execute code in internal `process:order-service`, but that process is explicitly issued the database credential and full read/write grant. Impact is high because the inherited grant reaches confidential `store:orders-db` records tagged `pii` and `financial`.

mitigations.summary: Apply least privilege to the order-service database role
mitigations.detail: Limit the application account on `flow:process:order-service>store:orders-db>read-write-orders` to the rows, columns, and operations required for order capture.
Log database queries by the order-service identity and alert on extraction volumes or query patterns inconsistent with normal order processing.
